subject: english-literature
title: Close Reading and Formalism
welcome_lead: Critical reading begins with close attention to the words on the page. Formalism and New Criticism gave us the disciplined tools.
meta_desc: English Literature: close reading, formalism, New Criticism, PEEL and PETER.
final_note: The text rewards patient attention. Read slowly, twice.

concepts.def: Detailed analysis of a passage's language, structure and devices.
A critical approach focused on form, structure and literariness.
Mid-20th-century US movement emphasising the autonomous text and ambiguity.
Point, Evidence, Explain, Link — an essay paragraph structure.
Point, Evidence, Technique, Explanation, Relevance — analytic paragraph structure.
William Empson's term for the productive multiplicity of meaning in literature.

walkthroughs.body_html: Identify devices, then explain their effect, then link to the wider thematic argument. Avoid simply listing techniques — interpret them.
Wimsatt and Beardsley warned against the intentional fallacy (judging by author intent) and affective fallacy (judging by reader response). For New Critics, the text speaks for itself.
Empson's Seven Types of Ambiguity argues that literary richness depends on multiple simultaneous meanings. Resist flattening a passage to one reading too early.
